mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC (from -45.1% to -37.6%, a 7.5 percentage point gain over three weeks) signals momentum in consumer confidence and foot traffic recovery. This trend will continue linearly into the next four weeks, producing higher mean RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 7.5 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or weekly improvements reverse for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -39.4% to -25.1% (14.3 point gain), indicating outdoor activity substitution is normalizing. As outdoor recreation demand stabilizes, consumers redirect discretionary spending back to indoor retail venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -30% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 14.3 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below -30% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station usage remains severely depressed at -73.0%, constraining commuter access to retail districts. If TRANSIT does not improve by at least 5 percentage points within two weeks, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed because foot traffic to retail hubs depends on transit connectivity.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -70% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -73.0% with minimal week-on-week change
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 percentage points in the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises above -30%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains depressed at -33.0%, indicating continued remote work or capacity restrictions. Weak workplace attendance suppresses daytime retail traffic and lunch-hour spending. RETAIL_REC will decline further if WORKPLACES does not recover by at least 8 percentage points within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -35% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -33.0% with minimal improvement trend
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -25% within four weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously exceeds -30%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has normalized to -1.0% (nearly baseline), indicating essential shopping is fully restored. When essential shopping normalizes while RETAIL_REC remains depressed at -37.6%, consumers are deliberately avoiding discretionary retail. This bifurcation will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -30% while GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline, indicating discretionary spending has decoupled from essential shopping normalization.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 20.1% to 18.0% over three weeks, signaling residents are spending more time outside homes. Combined with PARKS recovery (from -39.4% to -25.1%), this indicates outdoor mobility is increasing. As residents venture out more, retail venues will capture incremental foot traffic, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above 20% or PARKS falls below -30% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September in Madrid typically marks the end of summer holidays and return to school/work routines. RETAIL_REC improvement from -45.1% to -37.6% over three weeks aligns with this seasonal pattern. Continued seasonal normalization will drive RETAIL_REC toward -25% over the next four weeks as back-to-school and autumn shopping accelerates.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 7.5 points in three weeks ending mid-September
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve by at least 5 percentage points over the next four weeks, or falls below -40%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains severely depressed at -73.0% while WORKPLACES is at -33.0%, indicating a regime where commuting infrastructure is unavailable or avoided despite some workplace reopening. This mismatch prevents retail districts from receiving commuter foot traffic. RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed unless both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve simultaneously by at least 10 percentage points within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -73.0% and WORKPLACES at -33.0% with minimal convergence
failure_condition: Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by at least 10 percentage points within four weeks and RETAIL_REC rises above -30%.
